data.title: Certain Class A Common Stock of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. are subject to a Lock-Up Agreement Ending on 20-AUG-2026.
data.summary: Certain Class A Common Stock of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. are under a lock-up agreement set to end on August 20, 2026. This lock-up period, initiated on June 11, 2026, spans 70 days and affects approximately 911.5 million Class A Common Stock, which will be released on August 6, 2026, following the first earnings release on August 4, 2026. The founder's shares are subject to a longer 366-day lock-up, while other shareholders have varying release schedules tied to quarterly financial results and specific dates, with some shares having automatic early release provisions.

data.title: SpaceX Shares Drop 2.6% Amid 319 Million-Share Unlock in Thin Cash Market
data.summary: SpaceX shares (NASDAQ:SPCX) dropped 2.57% on Wednesday, closing at $139.65, as the market reacted to the unlock of an additional 319 million shares. This tranche represents 4.4 times Wednesday's trading volume and nearly half of the 638.9 million shares offered in June. Despite the drop, the stock remains 3.4% higher than its IPO price of $135, though it is 38.1% below its peak, with analysts divided on its valuation.

data.title: Can You Identify Winning Stocks in Advance?
data.summary: This article discusses Professor Hendrik Bessembinder's research, which reveals that only a small number of "superstar" stocks drive the majority of stock market wealth creation, with most individual stocks underperforming Treasury bills. The research indicates that these winning stocks are characterized by rapid growth in fundamentals, particularly income growth, and often experience significant drawdowns. The conversation also touches on the impact of private markets and global stock performance on this phenomenon.

data.title: SpaceX Stock Is Everywhere: Google, Nvidia, AMD, Harvard Disclose Stakes

These filings highlight broad institutional interest in Elon Musk's rocket company, though the reported data represents holdings as of quarter-end and may not reflect current market activity.

data.title: SpaceX completes acquisition of Anysphere in $60 billion all-stock deal
data.summary: SpaceX announced the completion of its $60 billion all-stock acquisition of Anysphere, Inc. (also known as Cursor). Anysphere shareholders received SpaceX Class A common stock and vested restricted stock units were converted into SpaceX shares, while unvested units and options were assumed by SpaceX. The transaction was structured to be exempt from registration requirements, and Anysphere will now operate as a wholly owned subsidiary.

data.title: SpaceX (SPCX): Founders Fund and Peter Thiel disclose 5.5% ownership stake
data.summary: A group of investment entities associated with Founders Fund and Peter Thiel has disclosed a collective beneficial ownership of 5.5% of SpaceX's (SPCX) Class A common stock. This stake, totaling 427,306,025 shares, was reported in a SCHEDULE 13G SEC filing as of June 30, 2026. Peter Thiel individually holds both sole and shared voting and dispositive power over a significant portion of these shares.

data.title: Why is Space Exploration Technologies stock sliding today?
data.summary: Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) stock is down today after the company confirmed the $60 billion all-stock acquisition of Anysphere, Inc., leading to the issuance of 389.3 million new Class A shares and significant dilution. This comes amidst exhausted short-covering momentum and looming sales of 319 million insider shares, contributing to a supply overhang. Valuation concerns, with SPCX trading at a 61x price-to-sales ratio and negative GAAP earnings, also weigh on the stock.

data.title: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) closes $60B Cursor deal in all-stock merger
data.summary: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) has completed its $60 billion all-stock acquisition of Anysphere, Inc. (Cursor), making Cursor a wholly owned subsidiary. The deal involved issuing over 389 million shares of SpaceX Class A common stock to Cursor shareholders and converting Cursor's restricted stock units and options into SpaceX equity, which will lead to some dilution for existing shareholders. The transaction was structured as an unregistered offering under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act, allowing SpaceX to preserve cash resources.

data.title: Elon Musk Discloses 48.4% Ownership Stake in SpaceX
data.summary: Elon Musk has revealed his beneficial ownership of 48.4% of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. through a Schedule 13G filing. This includes approximately 6.42 billion shares of SpaceX Class A common stock held as of June 30, encompassing shares held via trusts, restricted Class B shares, and options. The disclosure offers an updated view of Musk's significant stake in the aerospace company he established in 2002.

data.title: Elon Musk (SPCX) controls 6.42B as-converted SpaceX shares in latest 13G
data.summary: Elon Musk has filed a Schedule 13G indicating beneficial ownership of 6.42 billion as-converted Class A SpaceX shares, representing a 48.4% stake in the company. His holdings include Class A and Class B shares held by trusts, restricted Class B shares, and Class B options, giving him sole voting and dispositive power over these shares. Each Class B share carries 10 votes compared to one vote for Class A shares, significantly concentrating his control.

data.title: Pre-IPO Funds Slump After SpaceX Debut
data.summary: Pre-IPO funds, which experienced a boom earlier this year as retail investors sought exposure to private companies, are now seeing a slump following SpaceX's public debut and subsequent share lockup expirations. This trend has led to a significant decrease in the premiums at which these closed-end funds (like Robinhood Ventures, Fundrise, and ARK Invest) were trading, highlighting the volatility and concentration risk in this nascent retail-oriented investment strategy. Experts suggest that the influx of SpaceX shares after its IPO and a general "fear of missing out" by retail investors who bought at high premiums contributed to the current market shift.

data.title: xAI’s Neocloud Pivot Eats Up SpaceX Capital Expenditure
data.summary: Elon Musk's xAI is shifting its strategy from solely developing large language models to becoming an AI neocloud company, renting out access to AI infrastructure. This pivot, driven by stalled adoption of its Grok chatbot, has led to a significant increase in capital expenditures for SpaceX, with AI-related spending more than doubling in the second quarter of 2026. Despite the high costs, the move is showing early signs of success, with xAI achieving a $1.1 billion EBITDA gain primarily from GPU rental deals with clients like Anthropic and Google.

data.title: SpaceX Executive Says Starship Could Unlock Orbital AI Data Centers as Earth Faces Power, Land and Cooling Constraints
data.summary: SpaceX Vice President Stephanie Bednarek stated that Starship could enable large-scale orbital AI data centers, leveraging solar power in space to overcome terrestrial power, land, and cooling limitations. SpaceX plans to mass-produce AI satellites, similar to Starlink, and aims for initial orbital AI computing demonstrations by late 2027, with broader deployments starting in 2028. CEO Elon Musk believes space will soon be the most cost-effective location for extreme AI computing.

data.title: SpaceX Earnings: Stock Significantly Overvalued as Massive AI Investments Outweigh Hefty Neocloud Rent

The company's stock is considered overvalued, trading at twice its fair value, as investors are seen to be factoring in overly optimistic scenarios for Starship reusability and orbital datacenters. SpaceX's decision to exclusively use Nvidia chips for upcoming AI satellites and terrestrial datacenters, potentially signaling a shift from its own chip development plans, also raises questions about its long-term strategy.

data.title: SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX) Q2 revenue jumps 92% to $7.8B with AI surge
data.summary: SpaceX reported a significant Q2 2026 revenue increase of 92% to $7.8 billion, driven by strong performance in its Connectivity and AI segments, although the company remained unprofitable with a net loss of $541 million. The AI segment's revenue surged 247% year-over-year, reaching $2.6 billion, and achieved positive Adjusted EBITDA. SpaceX also strengthened its liquidity with $100 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, following a successful IPO and bond issuance, and announced an agreement to acquire Cursor for $60 billion.
